benchmark_validity_warning: This result is NOT a valid difficulty benchmark for this trainer. Shadow Tag did not prevent my switches (see defect 1), and Shadow Tag is the mechanical premise of the entire team. I switched three times - Weavile out at 21 HP on T3, Magearna away from a lethal Mirror Coat on T5, and a 1 HP Kartana on T6 - and every one of those should have been illegal. No level change has been made for that reason.

attempts.narrative: I played the anti-Wobbuffet line deliberately: single-target moves only, never feed the wall a big hit, and remove Swoobat before Simple Calm Mind turns over. T1 Weavile's Knock Off (2x on Psychic) KO'd Swoobat from full 87 before its Calm Mind resolved; Wobbuffet used Safeguard. T2 Knock Off broke Kadabra's Focus Sash and a critical Flash Cannon finished it, while Wobbuffet's Mirror Coat failed - I had not hit it with anything special. T3 I switched the 21 HP Weavile for Kartana (this should have been blocked) and Wobbuffet's Encore failed into the switch; Musharna Protected. T4 Flash Cannon at +3 Soul-Heart KO'd Musharna from full 129 and Wobbuffet's Counter failed. T5 Kartana's Smart Strike finally drew the Counter - 84 damage, saved only by its Focus Sash - and I moved Magearna out of Mirror Coat range. T6 Air Slash flinched Wobbuffet. T7 Ice Beam finished it.

strategy_checks.evidence: Three successful player switches with an alive Wobbuffet whose ability the state reports as ABILITY_SHADOW_TAG, and the driver reported may_switch: true every time. My party contains no Ghost-type and no Shed Shell. See defect 1 for the exact cause.

strategy_checks.check: Shadow Tag does not redirect attacks
strategy_checks.evidence: Every attack I aimed at Swoobat, Kadabra and Musharna landed on its chosen target. Shadow Tag never pulled an attack onto Wobbuffet. The 'crack' line's warning holds.

strategy_checks.check: Wobbuffet Encores a completed support move
strategy_checks.evidence: Encore was selected once, on T3, aimed at Weavile - which switched out, so it failed outright. It was never aimed at a support move; by T3 the only moves I had used were Knock Off, Thunderbolt and Flash Cannon, all attacks, so there was no 'completed support move' to lock. The authored condition had no valid instance in this battle.

strategy_checks.check: Wobbuffet Safeguard against a relevant status line
strategy_checks.evidence: Safeguard went up on T1 and expired on T5 without ever preventing anything. My six carry zero status moves, so there was no status line to guard against. The AI could not know that - nothing of mine was revealed on T1 - but the authored condition ('against a relevant status line') was not met, and the move burned the one proactive turn Wobbuffet had.

strategy_checks.check: Counter and Mirror Coat punish the matching damage category
strategy_checks.evidence: Mirror Coat on T2 failed, Counter on T4 failed, Counter on T5 landed for 84 damage into Kartana (saved only by a Focus Sash), Counter on T6 was flinched away. One success in four attempts. The single success was excellent and was the only damage Jaclyn's team dealt all battle.

strategy_checks.check: Swoobat Simple Calm Mind into Stored Power
strategy_checks.evidence: Swoobat selected Calm Mind on T1 - the correct opener - and was KO'd from full 87 HP by a single Knock Off before it resolved. Stored Power never fired. The team's SETUP flag never produced a single boost.

strategy_checks.check: Kadabra supplies immediate speed behind Magic Guard and Focus Sash
strategy_checks.evidence: It used spread Dazzling Gleam on the turn it entered, 2x on Weavile for 61 and correctly resisted by Magearna. Focus Sash held once. That is the whole of what a Kadabra in this slot can do and it did it.

strategy_checks.check: Musharna uses Yawn or direct damage rather than redundant setup
strategy_checks.evidence: It Protected on T3 and selected Psychic on T4 (KO'd before it resolved). It never used Yawn. No redundant setup was attempted, so the authored replacement of reserve Calm Mind with Yawn at least did not misfire - but Yawn was also never demonstrated.

protect_ledger.payoff: REAL BUT SMALL: blocked one Flash Cannon from a +2 Magearna, which is meaningful damage on a 129 HP body. It did not save Musharna's life - the same attack at +3 KO'd it from full the following turn - so the guard bought one turn that the team then did nothing with.

protect_ledger_note: One opponent Protect in seven turns. Not empty, not repeated, but also not converted into anything.

ai_defects.board: An alive opposing Wobbuffet with ABILITY_SHADOW_TAG on the field, my battlers Dark/Ice (Weavile), Steel/Fairy (Magearna) and Grass/Steel (Kartana), none holding Shed Shell, none Ghost-type.
ai_defects.chosen: The driver reported may_switch: true and accepted all three switch commands.
ai_defects.why_wrong: Shadow Tag should have made every one of those switches illegal. This is not an AI scoring problem - it is a legality gap in the headless driver's switchability report. src/emerald_champions_agent_battle.c:415 computes switchability as '(!IsBattlerAlive(battler) || CanBattlerSwitch(battler)) ? 0x100 : 0'. CanBattlerSwitch (src/battle_script_commands.c:3204) only walks the party looking for a healthy, non-egg, not-already-on-field member; it performs no escape check at all. The native player menu applies the missing check separately, at src/battle_main.c:3758 and :4055, by calling IsAbilityPreventingEscape (src/battle_util.c:5027), which is what actually implements Shadow Tag, Arena Trap and Magnet Pull. The agent path never calls it. Note that the source comment immediately above line 415 - 'A fainted battler owes a replacement; trapping does not apply to it' - shows trapping was considered for the fainted case and simply never implemented for the living case.
ai_defects.better_action: The agent switchability flag should mirror the menu: refuse the 0x100 bit when IsAbilityPreventingEscape(battler) is non-zero and the battler is alive and not holding a Shed Shell (and likewise for the escapePrevention volatile from Mean Look / Block / Spider Web).
ai_defects.note: Scope beyond this battle: this silently disables every trapping benchmark in the campaign for any agent driven through the headless driver - Shadow Tag, Arena Trap and Magnet Pull alike. Eddie in play_order 53 also fields an Arena Trap Dugtrio; there it happened not to matter because Dugtrio died on turn 2 and my only switch came afterwards, but the same gap was present. I have not touched the file - it is the driver, and the brief says not to hack it.

ai_defects.board: Wobbuffet on the field for six turns against a party that used only attacking moves.
ai_defects.chosen: Safeguard (T1), Mirror Coat (T2, failed), Encore (T3, failed), Counter (T4, failed), Counter (T5, landed), Counter (T6, flinched).
ai_defects.why_wrong: Five of six turns produced literally no effect. I am recording this as a defect of expected-value calibration rather than of any single choice, because each choice in isolation is arguable: Encore and the reactive moves are gambles, and on T1 nothing of mine was revealed. But by T4 the AI had watched me use four attacking moves in a row and had taken exactly one special hit and zero physical hits, and it still chose Counter - the move that requires a physical hit - twice in a row. The information needed to prefer Mirror Coat there (last used moves, revealed sets) is information the AI is explicitly allowed to use.
ai_defects.better_action: On T4, Mirror Coat rather than Counter: every attack I had landed on Wobbuffet up to that point was special, and Magearna was the only unrevealed-category threat on the board.
ai_defects.note: Related to the Sucker Punch pattern in play_order 50 and 54 - reactive moves whose precondition the board makes unlikely are being scored as though the precondition were even money.

ai_notes: Reporting bug, not gameplay: the driver emits MOVE_COUNTER as the string 'MOVE_68' in both state and events.jsonl (MOVE_COUNTER = 68 in include/constants/moves.h). Every other move in this battle resolved to a proper name. Something in the driver's move-name table is missing that entry, which makes Counter invisible to anyone grepping logs by name. Worth fixing before the next block reads Protect/Counter ledgers out of the logs.
Kadabra's spread Dazzling Gleam and Wobbuffet's one successful Counter were the only two things that hurt me. Both were correct.
calibration: Zero player faints in seven turns, which would normally trigger +1 on the weakest one or two members. I am deliberately NOT applying it. Shadow Tag - the mechanic this entire team is built around - was not enforced, and I used three switches that should have been illegal, including one that saved a 21 HP Weavile and one that took Magearna out of a lethal Mirror Coat. Raising levels to compensate for a disabled mechanic is exactly the thing AGENTS warns against ('Fix AI defects before compensating with levels'). This trainer should be replayed once the driver's switch legality matches the native menu, and calibrated from that run.
could_this_be_cooler: The concept is strong and unusually thoughtful - a trapper that punishes both damage categories, a Simple setter that converts one free turn into a sweep, and a Magic Guard sash lead - and I would keep all four species. Two observations. First, Wobbuffet's kit is almost entirely reactive: Counter, Mirror Coat and Encore all need the opponent to do something specific, and Safeguard needs the opponent to own status moves. Against a party of pure attackers it has no proactive line at all, which is how it spent five of six turns doing nothing. Once trapping actually works that changes a lot - the threat of being unable to switch is what makes a player walk into Counter - so I would re-evaluate rather than redesign. Second, Swoobat is the team's declared win condition and it is the frailest thing on the roster at 87 HP with no defensive investment; a Focus Sash on Swoobat instead of the Sitrus would guarantee the one Calm Mind the whole plan needs, and would cost nothing thematically. Neither is a level change, so nothing was touched.
